title: Sanity Suite: FP8/INT8 Golden-Seed Roller and Signal Integrity Checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need an automated, low-cost sanity suite that runs after model onboarding and after quantization jobs to catch subtle accuracy regressions introduced by FP8/INT8 profiles or calibration changes. The proposed 'Golden-Seed Roller' is a deterministic replay + randomized-seed stress harness that validates output signal integrity across: (a) top-k token overlap for generative prompts, (b) embedding cosine distributions for representation tasks, (c) end-to-end task pass rates for a small set of downstream checks (QA answer correctness, classification F1), and (d) key internal signals like KV-cache divergence and attention-score drift. This ticket covers the orchestration, metric thresholds, CI gating, and dashboard integration for the suite.
acceptance_criteria: Sanity suite runs end-to-end on CI for a quantized model artifact and completes within 25 minutes on a single dedicated CI GPU shard
Defines and implements three gating metrics with thresholds: top-1 token overlap >= 92%, mean embedding cosine >= 0.975, and downstream QA exact-match delta <= 3 percentage points
Generates a structured report JSON with per-prompt diffs, metric histograms, and a pass/fail boolean exposed to rollout pipelines
Implements a deterministic golden-seed replay mode and a randomized-seed stress mode; both modes included in nightly and pre-release runs
Dashboard panel added to Console QA workspace linking runs, with drift alerts for repeated failures over 3 consecutive runs
steps: Design metric suite and gating logic (lead: Liam) — finalize numeric thresholds, aggregation windows, and per-prompt severity weights
Assemble golden prompt set (2k tokens total across 150 prompts) with metadata: task, sensitivity, and seed behavior
Implement runner: Python harness that loads model artifacts (float32/FP8/INT8 variants), runs prompts with identical RNG seeds, collects token logits, embeddings, attention maps, and KV snapshots
Build comparison layer: compute top-k overlap, embedding cosine distributions, KL between probability vectors, and a lightweight task verifier for QA/classification prompts
Integrate with CI: add step to candidate-merge pipeline to invoke harness and fail merge on gate violations; add nightly cron for randomized-seed stress runs
Expose results as JSON artifact and push to Console metrics backend; create Dashboard panel and Slack alerter for failures
Create runbook for investigating failures: diff heuristics, sensitivity checklist (seed variance, batch shape differences, quant calibration mismatch), and rollback guidance
implementation_notes: Use per-channel calibration stats where available; compare per-tensor fallback to evaluate sensitivity to calibration granularity
For speed, use prefix caching and replay to avoid recomputing identical prefixes across variants; isolate final-token divergences
Randomized-seed mode should run with 20 different seeds seeded from a golden master to surface nondeterministic failures
We should capture hardware and kernel metadata (CUDA/cuDNN/hip versions, kernel selectors) in the run artifact to correlate environment-induced drift
Keep the golden prompt family small but diverse: long-context mathematical, instruction, dialogue, and factual recall examples to catch different failure modes
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tight numeric thresholds reduce false positives but may block deployments for benign stochastic variance; thresholds chosen to balance sensitivity and noise
A larger golden set increases coverage but makes the suite slower and harder to run on every PR; we split into smoke (CI) and extended (nightly) sets
Embedding cosine is sensitive to small-scale vector shifts; complement with downstream task checks to measure user-facing impact
Kernel/hardware nondeterminism may show as failures; we will surface environment details and add a quarantine workflow to avoid noisy alerts
